newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $61, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $61, passed - feedlots.

text.p: Feedlot cattle in the U.S. central and southern Plains were lightly bid early Wednesday at $61.00 per cwt but the bids were passed by owners asking $62.00 to $63.00, feedlot sources said.
Most of this week's sales so far have been at $62.00, although there were sales late Tuesday at $61.00, which was down $1.00 from Monday and down $2.00 from last week.

Some of the cattle sold at $61.00 were of lesser quality than animals that sold at $62.00, but others at $61.00 matched the same quality and were sold by feedlots which needed to move cattle to remain current, sources said.
Feedlots need to remain current because of outlooks for expanded cattle supplies through July, they said.

Although owners lost an average of $60.00 to $65.00 per head at this week's $61.00 per cwt cattle price, they stood to lose even more if market-ready supplies started backing up, several cattle feeders noted.

So far this week, feedlots in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area have sold out or were close to selling out their showlists, while Kansas feedlots generally still had cattle to sell, sources in those areas said.
